# Viva notes - read the code once and answer in YOUR words

**1. What is the ML problem?** Binary classification (placed / not placed) from 10 student features, plus
regression for the expected salary of placed students.

**2. Which dataset? (be honest)** A synthetic dataset of 1500 students generated by ml/data/generate_dataset.py,
because we had no real placement records. Placement is drawn from a noisy logistic rule (CGPA, skills,
internships help; backlogs hurt). So our metrics show how well the models learn that pattern. With real
data we would simply replace the CSV and retrain - the pipeline stays the same.

**3. Why synthetic data is still useful.** It lets us build and test the full pipeline (split, tuning, metrics,
integration into the website) end to end; the features match exactly what the website collects.

**4. Why a train-test split?** To evaluate on unseen data. 80/20, stratified so the placed ratio is the same in both.

**5. Which algorithms?** Logistic Regression (simple, probability output), Decision Tree (explainable rules),
Random Forest (many trees), Gradient Boosting (trees that fix earlier mistakes). Compared on the same split.

**6. GridSearchCV and cross-validation?** The training set is split into 5 folds; each parameter combination is
scored on held-out folds. The test set is never used for tuning (no data leakage).

**7. Why was Logistic Regression best?** Because the synthetic rule is logistic, a logistic model fits it best
and the dataset is small/noisy, so simpler models generalise better. On real data the winner could differ.

**8. Metrics?** Accuracy, precision, recall, F1, confusion matrix, ROC-AUC (see ML Lab tab). Precision = of predicted
placed, how many were. Recall = of actually placed, how many found. F1 = balance.

**9. Why not 100% accuracy?** The data has noise (random outcome), so even the best model cannot be perfect.

**10. How is the model used in the website?** Flask loads model.joblib; /api/ml-predict takes the profile and returns
probability, expected salary and a "why" explanation (each feature set to the training median to see its effect).

**11. Rule-based score vs ML model?** The rule-based score is a hand-made weighted formula; the ML model learns
from data. The ML Lab shows both for the same profile.

**12. Limitations.** Synthetic data, no real hiring factors, small feature set, results will change with real data.

**13. Future work.** Real placement records from the college, more features, XGBoost, SHAP explanations, deployment.

Tip: open placement_ml.ipynb, run it, then change one thing (test_size, max_depth) and see what changes.
